title: Euro stablecoins get a mainstream push as Revolut begins rolling out EURR in Europe
dek: Revolut has begun phased rollout of EURR, an EU-regulated euro stablecoin issued by Bridge, across Denmark, Poland, and Portugal. The launch signals fintech integration of stablecoins within regulated EU payment ecosystems.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: Revolut is rolling out EURR, Bridge-issued and EU-regulated, to a select group of customers in three European countries, marking mainstream fintech adoption of euro stablecoins on multiple blockchains.
bottom_line: Watch whether Revolut expands EURR availability beyond the initial three countries and the timeline for that expansion. If the rollout accelerates and other EU fintechs launch competing euro stablecoins, regulatory clarity around stablecoin issuance under EU law may be solidifying faster than previously expected, with implications for both fintech strategy and central bank digital currency adoption timelines in Europe.
body:
Revolut has begun a phased rollout of EURR, an EU-regulated euro stablecoin, to select customers in Denmark, Poland, and Portugal. The stablecoin is issued by Bridge, according to CoinDesk, and represents a significant integration of stablecoins into a mainstream fintech application operating across the European Union.
CoinDesk reports that Revolut is initially bringing EURR to a select group of customers within the three named countries, with the company controlling the pace and scope of availability as adoption proceeds. The limited initial launch is typical for stablecoin rollouts in regulated jurisdictions, where fintech companies often test systems and compliance workflows with constrained user cohorts before expansion.
This multi-chain approach has become standard for EU-regulated stablecoins seeking to maximize interoperability and avoid lock-in to a single network.
The stablecoin's regulatory status within the EU is central to Revolut's strategy. Bridge's issuance of EURR under EU regulatory frameworks positions the product differently from unregulated stablecoins operating in European markets. The regulatory designation shapes both the legal standing of the stablecoin as a store of value and the conditions under which Revolut can promote it to its European user base.
Revolut's adoption of EURR follows broader fintech moves to offer euro-denominated digital assets. The company operates payment and investment products in the EU under a fintech license framework, and the stablecoin addition extends that product range into on-chain euro access.
